blocks.text: Ask any poultry farmer in Ogun State why he doubled his flock last year and the answer will be short: the price of eggs went up. Producers respond to price in the opposite direction to consumers — and that single fact is the law of supply.

blocks.markdown:
**Supply** is the quantity of a commodity that producers are willing and able to offer for sale at a given price, over a given period of time.

Notice that supply is not the same as stock. A trader may have 500 bags of rice in his warehouse — that is stock. What he is prepared to sell this week at today's price is supply.

blocks.title: Law of supply
blocks.text: Other things being equal, the higher the price of a commodity, the greater the quantity supplied; and the lower the price, the smaller the quantity supplied. Price and quantity supplied therefore move in the same direction, which is why the supply curve slopes upwards from left to right.

blocks.caption: A supply schedule for eggs. Plotted, it gives a supply curve rising from left to right

blocks.markdown:
### Why supply rises with price

A higher price makes production more profitable, so existing producers expand output and new producers are drawn into the industry. A higher price also covers the rising marginal cost of squeezing extra output out of a fixed factory or farm, so units that were not worth producing at the low price become worth producing.

items: **Cost of production** — dearer feed, fuel or labour reduces supply at every price.
**Technology** — better incubators, improved seed or mechanisation increases supply.
**Government policy** — a subsidy increases supply; an excise tax or an export ban reduces it.
**Number of producers** — more firms entering the industry increases market supply.
**Weather and natural conditions** — a flood or a drought cuts agricultural supply sharply.
**Price of related goods** — if the price of maize rises, farmers switch land out of cassava, so cassava supply falls.
**Expectation of future prices** — expecting a price rise, sellers withhold stock today.
**Objectives of the firm** — a firm chasing market share may supply more than pure profit maximisation would suggest.

blocks.markdown:
### Movement along versus shift of the supply curve

As with demand, the good's *own price* produces movement **along** the curve: an **extension** of supply when price rises and a **contraction** when price falls. Every other determinant shifts the **whole curve** — rightward for an increase in supply, leftward for a decrease.

### Types of supply

**Joint or complementary supply** occurs when producing one good automatically produces another: beef and hides, crude oil and natural gas, cotton lint and cotton seed. **Competitive supply** occurs when the same resources could produce either good, so producing more of one means producing less of the other, as with maize and cassava on the same hectare.

items: **Highly perishable goods** — a fish seller at 6 p.m. will sell at any price rather than let the catch rot, so a falling price may not reduce the quantity offered.
**Fixed or unique supply** — an original painting or a fixed quantity of land cannot be increased however high the price rises.
**Backward-sloping supply of labour** — beyond a point, higher wages lead some workers to choose more leisure and offer fewer hours.
**Expectation of a price fall** — sellers may increase sales now even as the price falls, to avoid a worse price later.
**Agricultural output in the very short run** — once a crop is planted, this season's supply cannot respond to price at all.

blocks.title: Tracing the effect of a cost change on supply
blocks.prompt: The Federal Government removes the subsidy on poultry feed, so feed prices rise by 40 per cent. Using the egg supply schedule above, explain what happens to supply and how the schedule changes.

steps.text: Identify what changed. It is a cost of production, not the price of eggs, so the whole supply curve must shift rather than a movement along it.
Decide the direction. Higher costs make each crate less profitable, so at every price farmers are willing to supply fewer crates. Supply decreases and the curve shifts to the left.
Show it in the schedule. Where 50 crates were supplied at ₦3,000, perhaps only 38 are now supplied at that same ₦3,000.
Note the effect in the market. With demand unchanged, the leftward shift of supply raises the equilibrium price and lowers the equilibrium quantity of eggs.
State the general rule: anything that raises unit cost shifts supply leftward; anything that lowers unit cost shifts it rightward.

blocks.answer: Supply decreases: the whole supply curve shifts leftward, so less is offered at every price and the equilibrium price of eggs rises

blocks.title: Separate stock from supply
blocks.text: Examiners set traps here. Total stock is everything in existence or in the warehouse; supply is the part offered for sale at a stated price in a stated period. Hoarding is exactly the case where stock is large while supply is small.

points: Supply is the quantity producers are willing and able to sell at a given price in a given period.
The law of supply: price and quantity supplied move in the same direction, ceteris paribus.
Own-price changes give extension or contraction along the curve; other factors shift the whole curve.
Supply is determined by cost, technology, government policy, number of producers, weather, related prices and expectations.
Joint supply produces two goods together; competitive supply means more of one implies less of the other.
Perishables, fixed supply, the backward-sloping labour supply curve and very short-run farm output are exceptions to the law.
